title: Land use and land cover change effect on surface temperature over Eastern India

settings.description: Odisha state, 81-88 E and 17-23 N, analysed from 1981 to 2010 with 29 IMD stations, IMD and University of Delaware gridded temperature, and NCEP-NCAR Reanalysis-1.
The 1981-1990 decade, over which mean temperature below 500 m fell and the diurnal temperature range rose.
The 1991-2000 decade, over which temperature rose by about 1 C.
The 2001-2010 decade, the focus of the LULC attribution because validated LULC and EOS-era satellite products are available.
Stations below 500 m above mean sea level, the plains subset used for most decadal statistics.
High-altitude stations above 500 m, analysed separately and showing smaller trends.
December-February season, evaluated separately in the decadal trend analysis.
March-May season, evaluated separately in the decadal trend analysis.
June-August season, evaluated separately in the decadal trend analysis.
September-November season, evaluated separately in the decadal trend analysis.
Analysis repeated with extreme ENSO years 1982, 1983, 1997 and 1998 removed.
Observation minus reanalysis analysis at 0.5 degree resolution, using NNR which does not assimilate surface temperature, moisture or winds.
AWiFS 1 km land use and land cover classification compared between 2004 and 2010, aggregated to 10 km.
MODIS-Terra NDVI trends for 2001-2010, annually and by season.
District headquarters, in particular Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, where the OMR share of observed warming is quantified.
NCEP CFSv2 latent and sensible heat flux changes over 2001-2010 at 30 km resolution.

claims.statement: The state warmed by about 0.3 C over 1981-2010, with the most accelerated warming of about 0.9 C in the recent 2001-2010 decade.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. The headline thirty-year trend is absent; only the decade-to-decade contrast was captured.

claims.statement: Mean temperature below 500 m fell by about 0.7 C in 1981-1990 and rose by about 0.8 C in 2001-2010, a reversal of sign between decades.
claims.match_note: Extracted as the decadal contrast with both magnitudes.

claims.statement: The 1991-2000 decade shows an increase of about 1 C, the largest of the three decades.
claims.match_note: Not extracted; the middle decade is missing from the claim record even though a context exists for it.

claims.from: station location, coastal or inland, and altitude
claims.to: sign of the surface temperature trend
claims.statement: The surface temperature trend is positive irrespective of whether the station is coastal or non-coastal and of altitude, significant at 95 per cent in most cases.

claims.to: minimum temperature trend in the recent two decades
claims.statement: Minimum temperature decreased during 1981-1990 while maximum temperature rose, then increased by about 1.2 C over the two recent decades against about 0.13 C for maximum temperature.

claims.to: subsequent decadal diurnal temperature range trend
claims.statement: Diurnal temperature range rose by about 1.16 C during the 1980s then fell by about 0.46 C and 1.19 C in the two following decades below 500 m.
Overall trends are larger for low altitude stations than for those at higher altitudes.
Results computed with and without the extreme ENSO years 1982, 1983, 1997 and 1998 are consistent.
Between 1981 and 1990 temperature fell by 0.3 to 0.9 C depending on season, and the region has warmed by about 0.4 to 0.9 C since 1991 on the same seasonal basis.
claims.match_note: Extracted as the seasonal reversal with both ranges.

claims.statement: The largest rate of temperature increase occurs in JJA and SON and the smallest in DJF.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, although four seasonal settings were evaluated.

claims.to: relative rate of minimum versus maximum temperature increase
claims.statement: Irrespective of season, minimum temperature has increased much faster than maximum temperature since 1991.

claims.to: spatial pattern of the diurnal temperature range trend
claims.statement: Spatial patterns for mean, minimum and maximum temperature are similar across decades, while the diurnal temperature range shows opposing trends, rising in the 1981 decade and falling afterwards.
The increase in minimum temperature is more widespread spatially than the other temperature trends, which may indicate that climate change overwhelms LULC impacts at that scale.

The first decade shows a declining OMR trend of about -0.04 C per year, which the authors attribute to reanalysis dataset development rather than to land use and therefore exclude from further analysis.
claims.match_note: Extracted as the declining OMR trend.

claims.from: spatial pattern of increasing OMR trend
claims.statement: The highest increasing OMR trend of about 0.04 C per year coincides with Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, shifting from the west of the state to the east in the most recent decade.
claims.match_note: Extracted as spatial coincidence between the OMR pattern and urban centres.

claims.statement: The largest land use and land cover changes occur over the north-eastern part of the state.

claims.from: spatial pattern of land cover change 2004-2010
claims.to: spatial pattern of the OMR trend
claims.statement: The land cover change map matches the OMR trend map for the decade since 2001, giving independent confirmation that the OMR pattern reflects temperature change associated with land cover change.
claims.match_note: Not extracted as its own record, although it is the paper's central attribution argument.

claims.statement: Rabi crop cultivation increased by about 97 per cent at the cost of Kharif crops, showing agricultural diversification and changing cropping patterns.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, so the specific land-use transition driving the warming is absent from the graph.

claims.statement: Green vegetation decreased over the state, with a large NDVI decline especially over the eastern part.
claims.match_note: Not extracted as its own record; NDVI appears only as the source endpoint of the flux claims.

claims.to: spatial patterns of OMR and land cover change
claims.statement: The NDVI change pattern coincides with both the OMR pattern and the land cover change pattern, supporting attribution to changes in green cover and cropping.

claims.from: land use and land cover change
claims.statement: Between a quarter and a half of the observed warming since 2001 is associated with land use and land cover change, the higher figure applying over urban centres.
claims.match_note: Extracted as LULC-driven temperature rise concentrated in urban centres, though without the quantified share.

claims.statement: Cuttack and Bhubaneswar show OMR shares of about 40 and 50 per cent of observed warming over 2001-2010, and the rise is larger for larger cities than for smaller towns.
claims.match_note: Extracted as the enhanced urban LULC warming signature.

claims.statement: The decreasing NDVI trend is accompanied by an increasing sensible heat flux over eastern Odisha for 2001-2010.
The decreasing NDVI trend is accompanied by a decreasing latent heat flux over eastern Odisha for 2001-2010.
The observed decrease in latent heat flux favours warming over the eastern part of Odisha.
The observed increase in sensible heat flux favours warming over the eastern part of Odisha.

claims.from: LULC-induced warming rate in Eastern India
claims.to: rates reported for Eastern China, USA and Europe
claims.statement: The authors note that their rate of about 0.1 C per decade is comparable with rates reported for other rapidly developing regions.

notes: P000020_CL011 and P000020_CL012 record the generic relationships vegetation decrease to latent heat flux decrease and to sensible heat flux increase. In the source these appear only in the Physical mechanism paragraph as cited background ('It is known that ... LHF (SHF) increases (decreases) with increasing vegetation'), carrying references 3-5, 7, 8, 17, 23, 25 and 51-56. They should have been assigned CITED_BACKGROUND and discarded. They are deliberately left unmatched so the audit counts them as extracted claims without a reference, which is the precision signal for role misassignment.
